rationale: ROUND 2 of 7e2391ec-47d0-4820-afde-b4cc475714e5 (REVISE, gating objection from bug_historian) — every objection acted on, none defended. (1) THE GATING ONE WAS RIGHT AND FOUND A REAL DEFECT: a nil Evaluate result decoded to a zero-value scan and PASSED — the render audit's own '0 contrast failure(s) for a page it never measured' landmine reborn one rung higher. Fixed fail-closed three ways: the probe now stamps a sentinel (probe: 'contrast_ratio/v1') and the verdict REFUSES to grade any payload without it (nil, {}, and foreign payloads all fail with 'the probe did not run'); the probe counts elements actually measured (scanned) and a scan that measured zero text-bearing elements fails closed as vacuous rather than passing over nothing; Evaluate/decode errors were already explicit FAILs. Four new tests pin each path (nil, foreign payload, zero-measured, eval error). (2) bug_historian medium + guardian medium on the auditJS recomposition: string-contains was indeed weaker than needed — the test is now BYTE-IDENTITY against a golden of the pre-refactor literal, extracted MECHANICALLY from git (b32aa9cd9~1) into testdata, so a join-point defect (lost semicolon, duplicate binding, scope collision) cannot survive equality with a string that demonstrably executed in production; a deliberate future JS change must update the golden in the same commit, giving the audit's JS review visibility. (3) guardian medium / debug_historian medium on the TWO consumers: acknowledged and now stated everywhere — render-audit-adapter and browser-runner-adapter both build this package and run at different tags (the '80 tags behind' landmine); byte-identity makes the recomposition behaviourally inert for the audit at ANY tag, and the witness recipe names the GATING pod explicitly (kubectl -l app=browser-runner-adapter, grep -ac with positive+negative controls because the image has no strings binary — the recipe was already in the lane RUNBOOK, now cited in the plan as the objection asked). (4) editquality medium: the fragment-pinning test DOES exist as part of edit 5 (contrast_check_test.go TestAuditJSComposition) — round 1's sketch named it but under edit 5 not edit 3; now stated in both, and strengthened to the golden identity above. (5) editquality low (comment wording vs the case-literal harvest): the lockstep harvest regex is ^\s*case\s+"[a-z_]+" — it requires the case keyword at line start after whitespace, and every doc-block line begins with //, so a comment structurally cannot match; stated as the containment. (6) guardian low (MinRatio on the shared struct): this follows the struct's own established convention — MinWidth/MinHeight (has_visible_area) and ExpectValues (computed_values) are per-type fields on the same shared struct, and the P7 validator's experienceCheckTypeFields table refuses min_ratio on any other check type, which is the collision control the objection asks for. (7) reuse_agent low: toolContainer(doc, ch) IS the existing shared helper at run_checks_action.go:252 (per-check container, else document container, else the convention default) — reused verbatim by no_horizontal_overflow and this check; nothing re-derives containment. Everything else from round 1 stands: opt-in, unsafe default OFF, zero typed consumers (corroborated by the round-1 reviewers' own query), no fence or planner prompt names the type until the browser-runner-adapter rolls AND the check is witnessed failing vonc's real 1.66:1 eyebrow with a clean-page control.

plan.summary: Add a contrast_ratio Tier-4 check type to the browser-runner (round 2: fail-closed measurement identity added, golden byte-identity proof of the auditJS recomposition, two-consumer rollout stated). One in-page probe (the render audit's WCAG maths factored into one shared JS const) measures every visible text element's computed colour against its effective composited background; the verdict refuses to grade any result the probe did not stamp, refuses a vacuous zero-measured pass, fails on any FIRM failure (per-element WCAG AA 4.5/3.0 or explicit min_ratio), attributes the worst offender in/out of the tool container exactly as no_horizontal_overflow does, and never fails on over-image grounds. Vocabulary tables and lockstep tests move in the same change; no Tier-2 arm.

edits.rationale: The applicability allowlist and the execution switch make a check type real; the struct field is required because an unknown JSON key is dropped in silence (LANDMINES:8645). MinRatio on the shared struct follows the struct's own convention (MinWidth/MinHeight, ExpectValues) and the P7 type-fields table refuses it on every other type.
edits.sketch: case list gains "contrast_ratio"; evaluateOnPage gains `case "contrast_ratio": pass, detail, r := runContrastRatio(page, doc, ch, profile); addScoped(ch.ID, pass, detail, r)`; criteriaCheck gains `MinRatio float64 `json:"min_ratio"``; header doc-block line lists the type (comment lines begin // so the lockstep harvest's ^\s*case regex structurally cannot match them).

edits.rationale: Measurement in JS, verdict in Go (testable via the fakePage seam). FAIL-CLOSED IDENTITY (the round-1 gating objection): the probe stamps probe:'contrast_ratio/v1' and counts measured elements; the verdict refuses any payload without the marker (nil/{} / foreign all fail 'the probe did not run'), refuses scanned==0 as vacuous, and reports Evaluate/decode errors as explicit FAILs — a non-measurement can never read as a clean pass.
edits.sketch: contrastMathsJS = parseRGB/lum/ratio/over/effBG lifted VERBATIM from auditJS. contrastProbe embeds container (JSON-quoted), minRatio and the marker; same visibility/text filters as the audit; per-element need = large?3.0:4.5, minRatio>0 replaces both; records selector/text/fg/bg/ratio/need/overImage/px/inTool per failure. runContrastRatio: marker check -> vacuity check -> partition overImage (reported, never fails) -> fail on any firm failure, worst ratio = Culprit/CulpritSelector, detail carries the long pod-greppable marker sentence 'text is painted below its contrast threshold' + up to 5 named offenders + measured count; Scope tool/chrome/unknown from containment via the SHARED toolContainer helper (run_checks_action.go:252, the same one no_horizontal_overflow uses).

edits.rationale: Single-source the WCAG maths (two JS copies exist; a third would drift). TWO CONSUMERS ACKNOWLEDGED: browser-runner-adapter (Tier-4 gate) and render-audit-adapter (audit lane) both build this package and run at different tags — the '80 tags behind' landmine. Byte-identity (edit 5's golden test) makes the recomposition behaviourally inert for the audit at any tag: no coordinated rollout is needed because the composed string IS the string both binaries already run.

edits.rationale: Every verdict path proven against fixtures that could come out otherwise, INCLUDING the round-1 gating scenario (nil Evaluate result must fail closed — it previously passed) and the recomposition (byte-identity, not substring presence).
edits.sketch: Fail-closed: NilResultFailsClosed, ForeignPayloadFailsClosed, ZeroMeasuredFailsClosed, EvaluateErrorFails, BadShapeFails (a ratio arriving as a string is a payload-shape change, never a pass). Verdicts: PassesWhenClean (with measured count in the detail), FailsWithAttribution (pins the pod-grep marker sentence so a rewording breaks loudly), OverImageNeverFails, ChromeAttribution, ContainerNotFoundIsUnknownScope, WorstOffenderWins. plan.risks: 1) The fail-closed identity turns some infra flakes into check FAILs (an Evaluate timeout now fails the check explicitly) — deliberate: the alternative is the exact silent-pass the gating objection names; the detail strings distinguish 'could not measure' / 'probe did not run' / 'vacuous zero-measured' from a genuine contrast failure so a judge or human can triage without re-running. 2) The golden freezes the audit's JS: any deliberate JS change now requires a same-commit golden update — that is the point (review visibility on live fleet machinery), and the cost is one extracted file per deliberate change. 3) A page whose settled state genuinely has zero text-bearing elements now fails contrast_ratio — accepted: on this estate every Tier-4 page has visible text after settle, and a blank settle is itself a defect worth a red check. 4) Chrome failures still fail the check with Scope=chrome (the overflow precedent) — the judge routes by Scope; exempting chrome would silently pass text a person cannot read. 5) Still deliberately out of scope: seeds/planner prompts (Phase 2, only after the browser-runner-adapter roll + the vonc witness with a clean-page control), the render-audit lane's parked queue (bugs_open/296), Tier-2, and any vonc page repaint (gauntlet lane's surface).
